title: CivicCast claims-evidence registry schema (spec-claims-evidence-rule.md D2)
description: Structural contract for docs/claims/claims.yaml. This file documents the contract that scripts/policy/check_claims_evidence.py enforces by hand (stdlib + PyYAML only, no jsonschema dependency, matching check_release_truth.py's dependency posture) — it is the authoritative human/tooling reference for the shape, not a runtime-validated artifact.

governed_doc_set.description: D1: the enumerated set of docs within which every strong-claim token occurrence must carry an adjacent claim marker.

format.description: Marker grammar for this path: markdown uses `<!-- claim:ID -->`, python uses `# claim:ID` inside docstrings.

enforced.description: Whether the marker-scan check (D8 group 5) actively runs against this path in this slice. False entries document the D1-enumerated future governed set (README.md, CAPABILITIES.md, other docs/releases/*-verification.md) that ws3 intentionally does not yet sweep (D9: 'Not a repo-wide sweep; the RULE ships first').

claimId.description: Lowercase path-safe slug; matches the audit-control authority-record-v1 claim-id/control-id grammar family.

blob40.description:
Git blob ID, computed filter-aware via `git hash-object --path

` (the WS1 machinery).

typedInputs.description: D2: every role is mandatory. `verifier` ('checker script + registry schema', D2's own two-file description) and `fixtures` (exhaustively listed dependencies) are non-empty lists of roleFile. `code` (CC-WS3-005, round-3 audit) is EITHER a single roleFile OR a non-empty list of roleFile — a claim about evidence produced by several cooperating modules binds all of them; a single-module claim stays a bare mapping. Every other role is a single roleFile/testRole.

code.description: CC-WS3-005: one module (bare roleFile) or several cooperating modules (non-empty list of roleFile).

command.description: D4: the negative-control command definition (no committed result).

expected_red_when.description: D4: the condition under which this control must fail.

ci_safe.description: D4: true = this control RUNS inside the verifier job each time (same-run provenance) and is re-checked every run. False = not re-checked same-run by this verifier (historically resolved against a separate owner/auditor-signed authority record under D5; that external-evidence resolution requirement was removed 2026-08-07 — see check_claims_evidence.py's module docstring and CHANGELOG.md — so a ci_safe:false control's underlying claim still blob-drift-checks (D2) but this control itself is not independently re-verified).

resolution.description: Which resolution mode this claim was registered under. 'same_run': the D3 same-run verifier proves it every run. 'external_evidence': historically ALSO required an owner/auditor-signed authority record resolved against a separate audit-control repository (D5); that requirement was removed 2026-08-07 (owner decision — see check_claims_evidence.py's module docstring and CHANGELOG.md) as AI-invented ceremony the owner never asked for. Existing entries still carrying 'external_evidence' (docs/claims/claims.yaml) are unaffected structurally — parsing still requires at least one control with ci_safe:false, and D2 blob-drift binding still runs unconditionally against every one of their input roles — only the extra authority-record gate is gone.

claim.description: The exact claim asserted. Committed side: definitions only — never a run ID, artifact, or date (D2).

anchor.description: Heading text, bullet lead, or docstring bullet the claim marker is adjacent to; used by the stale-anchor check (D8 group 5).
